## Recommendation
- **Ratings for pier salmon this week (low confidence, none are pier reports):** St. Joseph 1, South Haven 1, Grand Haven 1, Muskegon 1. I'd expect slow pier fishing at all four.
- **Go to Grand Haven if you pick one.** It has the newest report, and it's the only port with a boat report from the last week.
- **Before you go, check the pierhead water.** I couldn't get live pierhead temperatures or a wind forecast. A sharp drop in surface temperature would be the upwelling sign that brings salmon to the pier (general guidance, Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension).
- **If the pier is slow, the boat fish are deeper.** Recent boat catches came 35-100 ft down in 60-120 ft of water, so plan on boats or the river if the pier stays quiet.
- **Lures:** on the pier, the past reports mention spoons, glow plugs, and nightcrawlers. Boats have been using green and orange spoons and white flasher flies (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).

## Why
- The most recent reports are all boat reports, so I can't rate the pier from this year's data.
- I'd expect the pier to be slow because the fish are holding 35-100 ft down, well offshore of the pier (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).
- I'd expect Grand Haven to be a reasonable first choice because its latest report (July 24) shows salmon being caught, while the other three ports' newest reports are from July 10.
- Past pier reports at these ports were slow in late summer: Grand Haven 2023-08-16 rated 0, and St. Joseph 2023-08-09 rated 1.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (boat only, June 18 to July 30):**
- Grand Haven, 2024-07-24: Chinook and coho boat fish 35-100 ft down in 60-120 ft of water, with green and orange spoons and white flashers working. Quality was not rated for Chinook and 1 (below average) for coho.
- Grand Haven, 2024-07-10: boat Chinook rated 2 (average), 40-100 ft down in 65-120 ft of water, with meat rigs and orange spoons.
- St. Joseph, 2024-07-10: boat Chinook and coho rated 4 (excellent) on spoons, 80-90 ft of water.
- South Haven, 2024-07-10: boat coho and Chinook rated 2, best at 75-80 ft and 105-110 ft of water, on rotators and flies.
- Muskegon, 2024-07-10: boat fish rated 2, 40-100 ft down in 70-120 ft of water, on meat rigs and flashers.
- No salmon pier reports appear for any of the four ports in this period.

**Past seasons (history, same surface temperature range, about 70 F):**
- Grand Haven pier, 2023-08-16: pier anglers casting spoons found the bite slow (0); glow spoons and plugs worked.
- Grand Haven pier, 2023-08-02: a few salmon on glow plugs (1).
- St. Joseph pier, 2023-08-09: pier fishing was slow (1); a few coho on nightcrawlers.
- Past boat reports at similar water temperatures commonly put fish 40-100 ft down in 70-150 ft of water (for example Muskegon, 2023-08-09).

**Conditions now:**
- The tool was in backtest mode, so I have no live data. The latest measured buoy surface temperatures are from the week before July 30: St. Joseph 73 F, South Haven 71 F, Grand Haven and Muskegon 68 F.
- I have no modeled pierhead temperature, no modeled cold-layer depth, and no wind forecast.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52-58 F, so with surface water at 68-73 F the salmon are likely deeper, near the cold layer.

## Caveats
- The newest report is 6 days old (Grand Haven, July 24). The other three ports' newest reports are 20 days old (July 10), so these ratings are guesses.
- The ratings are my expectations from boat reports and a few old pier reports. There are no current pier reports for any of the four ports.
- I could not check live pierhead temperatures, the upwelling signal, or the wind. Check those before you go.
- Boat results are a weak stand-in for the pier, since the boat fish are mostly well offshore.
